subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me a 40-word writing task in Spanish on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer for accuracy and range.
promptWeak: Give me a two-way translation drill (Spanish↔English) on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, with answers and the common mistakes to avoid.

questions.q: What does “el estrés me agobia” mean?
questions.explain: “Agobiar” means “to overwhelm/stress out”, so “el estrés me agobia” = “stress overwhelms me”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I'm keen on cooking”?
questions.explain: “Me apasiona” + infinitive = “I'm passionate/keen on”; “cocinar” = to cook (not “coser” = to sew).

questions.q: What does 'el billete de ida y vuelta' mean?
questions.explain: 'Ida y vuelta' means 'there and back', so 'el billete de ida y vuelta' = 'a return ticket'.
'El ocio' means 'leisure / free time'; it is a false friend with English 'office' (which is 'la oficina').

questions.q: What does 'soy aficionado al baloncesto' mean?
options: I am a fan of basketball
questions.explain: 'Ser aficionado a' means 'to be a fan of', so this means 'I am a fan of basketball'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I like playing the guitar'?
questions.explain: Instruments use 'tocar' (not 'jugar'); 'me gusta' + infinitive, so 'Me gusta tocar la guitarra'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I prefer reading to watching TV'?
options: Prefiero leyendo a ver la televisión
Prefieres leer a ver la televisión
Prefiero ver la televisión a leer
Prefiero leer a ver la televisión
questions.explain: 'Preferir A a B' uses infinitives: 'Prefiero leer a ver la televisión' = 'I prefer reading to watching TV'.
“Sacar notas” means “to get marks/grades”, so “sacar buenas notas” = “to get good marks”.

questions.q: Which means “If I studied more, I would pass”?

questions.explain: “El ajedrez” means “chess”; “el ajo” (garlic) is a near-miss distractor.
'El bienestar' literally means 'being well' and translates as 'wellbeing'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I do exercise to keep fit'?
options: Hace ejercicio para mantenerme en forma
Hago ejercicio para mantenerme en forma
Hago ejercicio porque estoy en forma
questions.explain: 'Mantenerse en forma' = 'to keep fit' and 'para' = 'in order to'; 'hago' is the correct first-person form.
“Mixto” = mixed, so “el colegio mixto” = “a co-educational school” (boys and girls).

questions.q: How do you say “I gave up sweets to be healthier”?
options: Dejé de comer dulces para estar más sano
Dejé de comer dulces para estar más enfermo
Dejo de comer dulces para estar más sano
Empecé a comer dulces para estar más sano
questions.explain: “Dejar de” + infinitive = “to give up/stop”, so “Dejé de comer dulces” = “I gave up eating sweets”.
